pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The person working at home
paragraphs: One flatmate needs predictable quiet for concentrated work in the evening. Calls in the shared room make that work difficult. The concern is the noise during work, not who the other person calls.
The flatmate is willing to discuss exceptions for urgent calls, provided they are told when an exception is needed. A smaller room and headphones are possible ways to reduce the disruption.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The person making calls
paragraphs: The other flatmate calls family members who live in different time zones. An earlier call is not always possible because the family must also be available.

They are willing to use the smaller room and headphones for regular calls. They also want a way to handle urgent calls outside the usual arrangement, rather than treating every late call as an emergency.

questions.prompt: What absolute promise does the caller avoid?
questions.answer: The caller won’t promise there will never be an urgent call
Exceptions could be communicated with a brief message
The underlying need is predictable concentration time, not control over family contact

pages.title: Raise a difficult issue
pages.instruction: You need quiet to work. Teacher needs late family calls. Discuss an arrangement that respects both needs

pages.title: Express preferences with would rather
pages.instruction: Use a base verb for your own preference and a past form for someone else’s present or future action

rows.subject: Another person’s action
rows.example: I’d rather you took calls in the other room

rows.subject: A negative preference
rows.verb: would rather + subject + didn’t + base verb
rows.example: I’d rather you didn’t take calls in this room

pages.note: The past form after I’d rather you refers to a present/future preference here. Would rather is not followed by to. Explain the practical need instead of treating the form as automatically polite.

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: A conditional agreement. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I can make the regular family call before ten thirty, using the smaller room and headphones. I’m willing to keep the shared room quiet after nine, provided we allow a brief exception for an urgent call and I message you if that happens. I’m not asking for unlimited late calls; I just don’t want us to treat an emergency as a broken routine agreement. Could you tell me whether that protects the concentration time you need? If the sound still carries, we can review the room arrangement rather than turn it into a judgement about either person’s consideration for others
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. I can make the regular family call before ten thirty, using the smaller room and headphones. I’m willing to keep the shared room quiet after nine, provided we allow a brief exception for an urgent call and I message you if that happens. I’m not asking for unlimited late calls; I just don’t want us to treat an emergency as a broken routine agreement. Could you tell me whether that protects the concentration time you need? If the sound still carries, we can review the room arrangement rather than turn it into a judgement about either person’s consideration for others.

s_mission.title: Two needs in one flat

questions.prompt: What makes quiet important to the first flatmate?
questions.answer: They do concentrated work at home in the evening.
questions.hint: Identify the activity that the calls interrupt.

questions.prompt: Why can’t every family call simply be moved earlier?
questions.answer: The family members live in different time zones.
questions.hint: Look for the constraint on the other flatmate’s schedule.

questions.prompt: Which two adjustments are both flatmates willing to discuss?
questions.answer: They are willing to discuss using the smaller room and headphones.
questions.hint: Find the room and the equipment in paragraph two.

referenceParagraphs: One flatmate does concentrated work at home in the evening and needs predictable quiet. The other calls family members in different time zones, so moving every call earlier is not always possible.
Both are willing to discuss using the smaller room and headphones. The person working also accepts that urgent calls may need an exception, provided the exception is communicated.

s_reply.title: The proposed arrangement

questions.prompt: Where will regular calls take place, and what equipment will the caller use?
questions.answer: Regular calls will take place in the smaller room, using headphones.
questions.hint: Find the room and equipment in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: When does the shared room’s quiet period begin?
questions.answer: The shared room’s quiet period begins at 9 pm.
questions.hint: Distinguish the quiet period from the 10:30 pm call deadline.

questions.prompt: What must the caller do when an urgent exception is needed?
questions.answer: The caller must send a message.
questions.hint: Look for the condition attached to urgent calls.

referenceParagraphs: For regular calls, the caller will use the smaller room and headphones and finish before 10:30 pm. The shared room will remain quiet after 9 pm so the other flatmate can work.
Urgent calls may be exceptions to the regular arrangement, but the caller must send a message when an exception is needed. The proposal does not remove the need to communicate.
